page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor is equipped with a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and Fast Multiply-Add. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2-highcpu-8 demonstrates average multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 7430.34 and a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34. However, single-core capabilities are relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.67. Memory bandwidth tests yield average results, achieving 412.9 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 48.32 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The instance performs moderately in specialized tasks, registering average scores in software compilation and text processing, but falls into the lower tier for image processing, ray tracing, and physics simulations.

With its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, the n2-highcpu-8 represents a cost-efficient option for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It achieves average throughput in database operations and static web serving, alongside 7.13 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Additionally, it supports light machine learning tasks, processing 415.57 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model. This profile makes the instance suitable for multi-threaded web serving, software compilation, lightweight database operations, and basic text processing pipelines, whereas memory-intensive applications or heavy single-threaded tasks may experience resource constraints.
